name: Soft-boiled detectives
description: This Constellation follows cosy mysteries where investigation is playful, social and a little strange. In these works, detectives question odd suspects, navigate anxious communities and solve cases where charm, humour and character matter just as much as the truth itself.

key_work.title: Frog Detective 2: The Case of the Invisible Wizard
key_work.brief_description: Another mystery is afoot in Frog Detective 2: The Case of the Invisible Wizard. In the town of Warlock Woods, a parade welcoming the Invisible Wizard has been mysteriously destroyed. As the ‘second-best detective’, players interview a new cast of low-poly characters and follow clues through gentle, comic conversation.

end.title: Duck Detective: The Secret Salami
end.brief_description: Solving crime is no walk in the pond. You are a down-on-his-luck detective who also happens to be a duck. Use your powers of de-duck-tion to inspect evidence, fill in the blanks, and bust the case wide open, in a narrative mystery adventure where nothing is quite as it seems.

end.title: Later Alligator
end.brief_description: Pat the alligator, a (mostly) harmless and (probably) innocent reptile is at the center of a conspiracy that could bring down the biggest, scariest family in Alligator New York City: his own! Explore the city, meet the Family, and try to save Pat before the clock runs out.

links.description: Later Alligator and Inspector Waffles</> build comic mystery worlds populated by anthropomorphic characters, but their tones are far apart. One is bright, anxious and puzzle-like, while the other borrows from noir, brightening crime fiction’s shadows through jokes and family-friendly investigation.

end.creator_credit: Gosho Aoyama, Kyokuichi-Tokyo Movie and TMS Entertainment
end.brief_description: The son of a world famous mystery writer, Jimmy Kudo, has achieved his own notoriety by assisting the local police as a student detective. He has always been able to solve the most difficult of criminal cases using his wits and power of reason.

links.description: Agatha Raisin and Detective Conan both make detection depend on noticing what others miss. One brings amateur curiosity to English village mysteries; the other turns a Japanese schoolboy detective into an anime hero, solving cases through observation, deduction and disguise.
